root_cause_label: Tool serialization leaks timeout/security_risk metadata into shell command strings throughout trajectory, preventing every meaningful install and execution attempt; agent never diagnoses the cause and drifts to a spec-violating non-RStan fallback before prematurely claiming completion
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent's tool call serializer repeatedly injects metadata fields (timeout, security_risk) directly into the shell command string, causing all rstan installation and script execution attempts to fail with exit code -1, and the agent never recognizes or corrects this root cause.
t_commit_evidence: The metadata injection pattern is established in step 4 and persists identically through steps 5, 7, 11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 21, 25, 26, 28, 31, 32, 35 — every substantive install/execute command fails with exit code=-1 or parse errors. The agent never issues a single clean bash command after step 3, so failure is locked in from step 4.
t_surface_evidence: Error: unexpected ',' ... Execution halted [The command completed with exit code 1.]
trigger_explanation: The agent's tool-call serialization mechanism consistently appends JSON metadata fields (timeout, security_risk) as literal text inside the quoted bash -lc string. This is a fundamental tool formatting defect: the agent generates command strings that are structurally malformed from the shell's perspective. Unlike a knowledge gap about the task domain, this is a code-generation failure where the model cannot produce syntactically valid tool invocations — every attempt follows the same broken pattern.
